answer: Belgium's itsme app ties one phone to one verified person: activation needs a Belgian eID card plus a matching bank account, both checked against the national register first. To forge one identity an attacker needs a stolen eID, a matching bank login, and the victim's phone — €2,000 in black-market parts plus a live victim, per account. One failed check locks the whole orchard of linked services, so mass-forged identities rot before earning a cent. A saffron grower cannot fake a harvest by relabelling crates; identity works the same way — one root, one name.
